summary.plain: COHERENT reports the first measurement of neutrinos scattering coherently off argon nuclei, using a 24-kilogram liquid-argon detector at Oak Ridge. The rate is consistent with the Standard Model; together with the earlier caesium-iodide result, the collaboration says it confirms the existence of the process.
summary.technical: First CEvNS measurement on argon using the 24 kg active-mass CENNS-10 liquid-argon detector at the SNS; two independent analyses each prefer CEvNS over the background-only hypothesis at greater than 3σ, with a flux-averaged cross section of (2.2 ± 0.7)×10^-39 cm^2 consistent with the Standard Model prediction. The collaboration states that the neutron-number dependence of this result, together with its earlier CsI measurement, confirms the existence of the CEvNS process and improves constraints on non-standard neutrino interactions.

title: First Measurement of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering on Argon
why_it_matters: Argon is a second, lighter target nucleus after CsI, so the pair of results traces how the CEvNS cross section depends on neutron number; the paper's introduction says this establishes the N^2 behavior predicted by the Standard Model. The introduction also notes that CEvNS from solar and atmospheric neutrinos forms the "neutrino floor" background in future dark-matter searches, which cross section measurements help quantify.
